harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as router between lan-a (node2, eth1, 10.60.10.0/24) and lan-b (node3, eth2, 10.60.20.0/24): added static interface addresses on node1's eth1/eth2, persistent ens7 addresses+routes on node2/node3 (Ubuntu 16.04, via /etc/network/interfaces.d), and a VyOS ipv4 forward filter with rule 5 (accept established/related), rule 10 (accept TCP/5432 from eth1->eth2 only), rule 900 (reject all else), default-action drop. Verified node2->node3:5432 succeeds while ping and other TCP ports are rejected. Completed the mandatory restart protocol on all three nodes sequentially (node1 router first, then node2, then node3), confirming changed boot_id on each and re-verifying the firewall policy and config persistence after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected topology: node1=VyOS with eth0(mgmt)/eth1/eth2, node2/node3=Ubuntu 16.04 with ens2(mgmt)/ens7
Determined eth1<->node2 and eth2<->node3 mapping via ping test on trial addressing
Configured node1 eth1=10.60.10.1/24, eth2=10.60.20.1/24 via VyOS configure/commit/save
Configured persistent ens7 addresses on node2 (10.60.10.2/24) and node3 (10.60.20.2/24) via /etc/network/interfaces.d, with 'up ip route' directives for cross-lan routes via node1
Verified ip_forward and per-interface forwarding already enabled on VyOS
Configured VyOS firewall ipv4 forward filter: rule 5 accept established/related, rule 10 accept tcp dport 5432 eth1->eth2, rule 900 reject all, default-action drop; committed and saved
Tested with nc listener on node3:5432 - confirmed TCP/5432 from node2 succeeds and payload received; confirmed ping and TCP/22 both directions rejected
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline on all 3 nodes

Restarted node1 via 'sudo reboot' (backgrounded so ack returned first), polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id, re-verified firewall rules/interfaces persisted, re-tested TCP 5432 allow / port22+ping reject
Restarted node2, polled until available, confirmed new boot_id, verified ens7 IP/route persisted, re-tested policy
Restarted node3, polled until available, confirmed new boot_id, verified ens7 IP/route persisted, ran final end-to-end test and checked VyOS rule hit counters incremented across all tests

evidence.summary: nc listener on node3:5432 received 'hello' payload sent from node2; VyOS rule 10 counter incremented to 1 packet

evidence.requirement: Reject all other traffic between lan-a and lan-b (baseline)
evidence.summary: ping and TCP/22 from node2->node3 and node3->node2 both rejected (ICMP port-unreachable / TCP connection-refused); VyOS rule 900 counter incremented to 4
Captured node1 interfaces, VyOS identity, boot_id 7668189d..., and committed firewall/interfaces config prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sudo reboot' acked immediately; subsequent execs timed out/reset while rebooting; node1 became reachable again with boot_id a0df7da9... (changed from 7668189d...)
Post-restart: firewall ruleset (rules 5/10/900, default drop) and eth1/eth2 addresses intact; TCP/5432 allowed, TCP/22 rejected confirming policy still enforced

evidence.requirement: node2 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered config
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 74fd91b6...; reboot acked; SSH connection-refused during reboot; boot_id changed to 5d16f7b6... after recovery; ens7 IP/route persisted; TCP/5432 allow and TCP/22 reject re-verified

evidence.requirement: node3 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered config
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id dca72801...; reboot acked (payload sent to nc listener just before, confirmed received); SSH connection-refused during reboot; boot_id changed to 844af368... after recovery; ens7 IP/route persisted; final TCP/5432 allow + ping/TCP22 reject test succeeded, payload received on node3

evidence.requirement: Final firewall rule-hit evidence after all three restarts
evidence.summary: VyOS rule counters after full restart cycle: rule5(established/related)=21pkts, rule10(tcp/5432)=3pkts, rule900(reject)=5pkts, default drop=0 — consistent with the allow/reject tests run across all three restart phases
